sentences.text:
THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR ORDERS THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioner/Accused No.2 has filed this petition seeking anticipatory bail in the event of his arrest in Crime No.22/2024 of Mysuru City Women Police Station, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 376, 354A, 504 r/w. 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 ('D.P. Act' for short).
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned HCGP for the Respondent-State.
Perused the records.
3. The complainant, who is the wife of Accused No.1 i.e., daughter-in-law of the petitioner has lodged a complaint by setting the law in motion.
Initially the complaint was registered for the offences under Sections 498A, 354A and 504 r/w. 34 of IPC and Sections 3 & 4 of the D.P. Act.

But,
subsequently in view of further statement of the victim/first informant, the offence under Section 376 of IPC came to be incorporated.
The allegation of the prosecution discloses that the marriage of the first information was performed with Accused No.1 on 25.02.2021 and sufficient dowry was paid on demand.
It is alleged that even after the marriage, the petitioner and other accused all along subjected the complainant to ill- treatment demanding additional dowry.
After the marriage, the complainant has received certain amount from her company, which she paid to her father.

But, in this regard the petitioner and Accused No.2 quarreled with the complainant and subjected her to ill-treatment and subsequently she was subjected to harassment under the pretext of not getting child.
Later on, it is alleged that the petitioner has also sought sexual favour from her by inducing her.
When the complainant is alleged to have brought it to the notice of her husband/Accused No.1, he did not trust her and in fact he subjected the complainant to ill-treatment.

It is also alleged that, in the absence of Accused Nos. 1 &
3, the petitioner has made several attempts to commit rape by sexually assaulting her and he used to insist her to stand in nude position before him to satisfy his lust and when the ill-treatment exceeded the NC: 2024:KHC:14896 limits, the complainant being unable to bear harassment,
lodged a complaint in this regard.
5. On the basis of the complaint, FIR came to be issued and the petitioner along with other two accused filed a petition seeking anticipatory bail before the learned Sessions Judge.

However the learned Sessions Judge has allowed the anticipatory bail petition of Accused Nos. 1 & 3 i.e, the husband and mother-in-law of the complainant and rejected anticipatory bail petition of the V Nataraja vs State Of Karnataka on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176028170/
2 petitioner, considering the serious allegations made against him.

sentences.text: 6. The allegation of the prosecution discloses that the petitioner being the father-in-law of the complainant, on number of occasions, attempted to rape her and insisted her to be in nude position before him, when the Accused Nos. 1 & 3 were not in the house.
It is alleged that, all along whenever she used to go for bath, the petitioner used to follow her and he tried to rape her.

The records also disclose that, though initially she lodged a complaint under Sections 354A and 498A of IPC,
subsequently when her statement was recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., she narrated the entire incident in detail NC: 2024:KHC:14896 and on the basis of her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., the Investigating Officer has sent a requisition to incorporate the offence under Section 376 of IPC.
The petitioner is the father-in-law of the complainant and his behavior should be befitting to his status.
But, here the allegations disclose that he expected sexual favour from his daughter-in-law.
This discloses the mentality of the petitioner and now the petitioner is seeking anticipatory bail.

7. Considering the seriousness of the allegations, if the petitioner is enlarged on anticipatory bail,
there is every possibility of he tampering the prosecution witnesses.
Considering the gravity of the offences, this is not a fit case, wherein the discretion can be exercised in favour of the petitioner.
Hence, the petition being devoid of any merits, does not survive for consideration.
Accordingly, the petition stands rejected.

Sd/-
JUDGE KGR*
